data.title: Alligator Bioscience signs agreement to sell mitazalimab to Biossil
data.description:
Lund, Sweden – Alligator Bioscience (Nasdaq Stockholm: ATORX), a biotechnology company whose principal asset is a financial interest in the HER2-targeting antibody program HLX22, today announced that it has signed an agreement to sell all rights and assets related to the CD40 agonist antibody mitazalimab to Biossil Inc. (“Biossil”). Alligator will receive USD 0.75 million upfront and is eligible for up to USD 108 million in milestone payments, as well as royalties on future sales.

Under the agreement, Biossil acquires worldwide rights to mitazalimab, including its derivatives, for all indications and uses, including patents, clinical and regulatory data, know-how, manufacturing materials and drug inventory. From closing, Biossil will be responsible for all further development, manufacturing and patent costs, and has committed to develop mitazalimab.

As consideration, Alligator will be paid USD 0.75 million as an upfront payment. The milestone payments consist of up to USD 3 million in total upon first regulatory approval in the US and EU.

In addition, Alligator is eligible for up to USD 105 million linked to worldwide net sales, and mid-single-digit royalty on worldwide net sales, capped at USD 250 million in total. All payments other than the upfront payment are contingent on future events and there can be no assurance that they will be received.

If Biossil sells or licenses mitazalimab to a third party within two years of the signing of the agreement, Alligator will receive a share of the proceeds from such transaction.

Alligator believes the transaction provides an attractive balance between near-term value realization and potential future upside through milestone and/or royalty-based consideration.

Completion of the transaction is subject to customary closing conditions, including the transfer of assets and documentation and receipt of required third-party consents. Closing is expected within 30 days of signing. The proceeds are expected to extend Alligator’s financial runway and support the execution of its strategic objectives.

The sale of mitazalimab is in line with Alligator’s previously communicated strategy to focus on its economic interest in HLX22, and ends Alligator’s costs for maintaining the mitazalimab program and related IP portfolio from closing.

“Mitazalimab has shown promising data in pancreatic cancer, and with this agreement it gets an owner that can take mitazalimab forward towards registrational trials. Importantly, Alligator, and thus our shareholders, keep a stake in the future value of the program,” said Søren Bregenholt, CEO of Alligator Bioscience.
“We thank Alligator for entrusting Biossil with continued development of mitazalimab,” said Alexander Mosa, CSO & Chair of Biossil. “Patients and investigators have invested time and hope in this therapy, which we will reciprocate with rigor and focus.”

For further information, please contact:

Søren Bregenholt, CEO

E-mail: soren.bregenholt@alligatorbioscience.com

Phone: +46 (0) 46 540 82 00

Johan Giléus, CFO

E-mail: johan.gileus@alligatorbioscience.com

Phone: +46 (0) 46 540 82 00

This information is information that Alligator Bioscience is obliged to make public pursuant to the EU Market Abuse Regulation. The information was submitted for publication, through the agency of the contact persons set out above, at 2026-10-31 08:15 CET.

About Alligator Bioscience

About Alligator Bioscience

Alligator is a biotechnology company that has historically focused on tumor-directed immuno-oncology. Following a strategic refocus, Alligator is prioritizing the value of its economic interest in HLX22, an anti-HER2 monoclonal antibody being developed by Shanghai Henlius Biotech Inc., from which Alligator is entitled to a share of revenues without incurring development costs. Alligator has discontinued further internal development of mitazalimab and in October 2026 agreed to sell the asset to Biossil Inc.

Alligator is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (ATORX) and headquartered in Lund, Sweden.

For more information, please visit alligatorbioscience.com.

About Biossil

Biossil is an AI-native drug development company advancing a pipeline of late-stage, first-in-class candidates for heterogeneous and life-threatening diseases. With teams in Toronto and Boston, and partnerships with leading academic medical centers and research hospitals, Biossil integrates proprietary AI with deep clinical and translational expertise to advance promising clinical-stage assets.

data.title: Apple’s Biggest Threat Isn’t Android — It’s AAPL's Own Devices, Analyst Says Ahead Of Q4 Earnings
data.description:
Key points:
  • Moffett said Apple’s appeal as a relative safe haven has been playing out for months, pushing the stock’s valuation to levels that leave less room for disappointment.
  • At roughly 36 times forward earnings, Apple’s earnings yield is only about 2.8%, he noted, which is roughly half the yield available in the Treasury market.
  • According to Moffett, the question heading into earnings may not simply be whether Apple delivers another solid quarter.

Apple Inc. (AAPL) heads into its fiscal fourth-quarter (Q4) earnings report with its stock near record levels and investors closely watching whether the company can sustain its momentum. However, MoffettNathanson co-founder and senior analyst Craig Moffett sees a less obvious risk emerging for the iPhone maker.

During an interview with CNBC, Moffett said Apple has increasingly been viewed as the “safe choice” among mega-cap stocks, helping drive a significant valuation premium. But with the stock trading at roughly 36 times forward earnings, he questioned whether investors have already priced in too much optimism.

Apple shares ended with a decline of more than 1% in Friday’s regular trade, but edged up by 0.1% in the afterhours session.

Apple’s ‘Safe’ Trade May Have Gone Too Far, Says Moffett

Moffett said Apple’s appeal as a relative safe haven has been playing out for months, pushing the stock’s valuation to levels that leave less room for disappointment.

At roughly 36 times forward earnings, Apple’s earnings yield is only about 2.8%, he noted, which is roughly half the yield available in the Treasury market. That makes the valuation particularly notable for a company whose shares have already rallied sharply this year by about 27%.

“It’s already priced in so much safety that you wonder whether it’s overshot somewhat,” Moffett said.

He pointed to Friday’s trading action as another potential warning sign, with Apple stock declining even as money flowed out of other mega-cap technology stocks, raising the possibility that investors could increasingly favor companies offering more attractive free-cash-flow or earnings yields.

According to Moffett, the question heading into earnings may not simply be whether Apple delivers another solid quarter. It is whether the company can produce enough growth to justify the premium investors are already paying.

Apple is set to report its Q4 results on Monday after the closing bell. Wall Street expects Apple to report earnings per share (EPS) of $1.98 on revenue of $113.25 billion, according to Fiscal.ai data.

Moffett Says Apple’s Biggest iPhone Threat May Be Device Users Already Own

Moffett also highlighted a more fundamental challenge for Apple as higher memory costs push up device prices.

He said higher memory costs have already lifted prices by about $100 across Apple’s base devices. U.S. wireless carriers, meanwhile, have not meaningfully increased promotions to offset those higher prices, meaning consumers are ultimately paying more, Moffett noted.

That creates a potentially bigger problem for Apple than losing customers to Android.

“The competition that Apple faces is from the Apple device that you already own,” Moffett said.

If consumers look at a new iPhone, see a higher price and decide their existing device still works well enough, they may simply delay upgrading, he said.

Moffett added that existing iPhones remain capable, run current software and can stay in use for years. As a result, higher prices could encourage consumers to stretch the replacement cycle, creating what Moffett called the “inertia” of the existing device.

Munster Remains Bullish On AAPL’s iPhone Duo

Last week, Deepwater Asset Management’s Gene Munster outlined his bullish outlook on Apple’s new iPhone Duo, forecasting 20 million units in FY27 versus Wall Street’s roughly 12 million estimate.

Munster expects the higher-priced device to add about $8 billion to the Street’s current FY27 iPhone revenue estimate of $279 billion.

He sees the Duo accounting for 8% of iPhone unit sales and 16% of revenue in FY27, well above Wall Street’s estimates of 4% and 7%, respectively.

Munster also expects Apple’s overall iPhone business to grow 13% in FY27, compared with the Street’s 10% forecast.

What Retail Traders Think Of AAPL Stock

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around Apple trended in the ‘extremely bearish’ territory at the time of writing.

AAPL stock is up 27% year-to-date and over the past 12 months. The S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) is up 11% over the past 12 months, while the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) is up 12%.

data.title: RBM Infracon bags order worth ₹354 crore; read more to find out
data.description:
RBM Infracon shares will be in focus on Monday after the company announced that it has bagged ₹354.76 crore order from Epitome Industries.

RBM Infracon Ltd has won a service order worth Rs 354.76 crore from Mumbai-based Epitome Industries India Ltd, the company told the National Stock Exchange in a regulatory filing on October 30.

The order, inclusive of all taxes and duties, was received by email on the same day. The company will provide design, engineering, construction, erection, testing and commissioning services for all buildings and structures under the contract.

RBM Infracon is expected to complete the project in 18 months.

The Ahmedabad-based infrastructure company has not said how the order compares with its current order book or annual revenue. Investors will watch for those details and for how quickly work begins in the coming quarters.

When we look at the stock performance, the share of RBM Infracom slipped to ₹189.30 after a sharp fall of ₹5.20, or 2.67%, on the last day of trading on Friday.

A quick look at the company's shareholding pattern reveals that 62% of the company's shares are held by the promoters; there are no holdings by FII or DII, and the remaining 37% is held by others.

data.title: Kwality Wall's Appoints Tahir Tanridagli As MD And CEO
data.description:
The appointment follows the company's separation from Hindustan Unilever, with Tanridagli set to lead its next phase of growth from November 1, 2026

Kwality Wall's (India) has appointed Tahir Toloy Tanridagli as its Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, effective November 1, 2026. The leadership change comes as the company enters its next phase of operations following its demerger from Hindustan Unilever Limited (HUL).

The appointment makes Tanridagli the head of India's largest listed pure-play ice cream business. The company's board approved his appointment following a recommendation from the Nomination and Remuneration Committee.

He will hold the position for three consecutive years, with his tenure scheduled to conclude on October 31, 2029. The appointment is subject to shareholder consent and other necessary statutory approvals.

Tanridagli To Lead Company's Next Growth Phase

Tanridagli is already a member of Kwality Wall's (India) Limited's board and has been involved in its post-demerger transformation.

As MD and CEO, he will be responsible for overseeing the company's overall management, business development and operational performance as it works towards its next stage of expansion.

In addition to his responsibilities in India, Tanridagli serves as President of the METSA region (Middle East, Türkiye, Africa, Israel and South Asia) at The Magnum Ice Cream Company (TMICC).

While he contributes to strategic direction at the regional level, his operational responsibilities in the new role will remain limited to the Indian business.

Kwality Wall's Announces Supply Chain Leadership Change

Alongside the CEO appointment, the company has also announced changes within its supply chain leadership.

Vivek Sarbhai will step down as Head – Supply Chain, India, and cease to be Senior Management Personnel from October 31, 2026. The company has attributed the change to a revision in his designation.

Ansu Archana will take over as Head – Supply Chain, India, and become Senior Management Personnel from November 1, 2026.

Archana brings more than 15 years of experience in supply chain management and procurement across multinational organisations. She has previously held director-level positions within Unilever's supply chain function.

She also played a key role in the separation of HUL's ice cream business and its transition into Kwality Wall's (India) Limited.

The appointments represent changes across the company's senior management and operational leadership as it establishes its organisational structure following the demerger.

The Magnum Ice Cream Company Holds 61.91 Per Cent Stake

Kwality Wall's (India) Limited operates as the Indian business of The Magnum Ice Cream Company, which describes itself as the world's leading ice cream business.

Following the separation from HUL, TMICC HoldCo acquired a controlling interest in the Indian company under a Share Purchase Agreement signed with Unilever in June 2025.

TMICC HoldCo currently owns a 61.91 per cent stake in Kwality Wall's (India) Limited.

The company's brand portfolio includes Kwality Wall's, Magnum and Cornetto. It is listed on both the BSE and the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

With the new appointments taking effect in November, Kwality Wall's is moving ahead with its leadership and operational structure as an independently listed business within the TMICC group.

data.title: Coal India Raises HRA For Non-Executive Employees, New Rates Effective Sept 1
data.description:
The revised allowance structure increases HRA to 27% for X-category cities, 18% for Y-category cities and 9% for Z-category cities, following the VDA revision to 26.8%

Coal India has revised House Rent Allowance (HRA) rates for eligible non-executive employees across the company and its subsidiaries, increasing the housing benefit in all three city classifications.

The revised rates will apply retrospectively from September 1, 2026, following an increase in Variable Dearness Allowance (VDA) beyond the threshold prescribed under the 11th National Coal Wage Agreement (NCWA-XI).

An office order issued by Coal India's Human Resources department on October 22, 2026, confirmed the revised allowance structure. The change will benefit employees covered under the applicable wage-board provisions, with the revised HRA calculated as a percentage of basic pay.

Check Revised HRA Rates Across City Categories

Under the updated structure, employees posted in X-category cities will receive HRA equivalent to 27 per cent of basic pay, compared with the earlier rate of 24 per cent.

For Y-category locations, the allowance has been increased from 16 to 18 per cent of basic pay. Employees working in Z-category cities will now receive 9 per cent, against the previous rate of 8 per cent.

The revised rates are as follows:

City classificationPrevious HRARevised HRA
X Category24%27%
Y Category16%18%
Z Category8%9%

The revision translates into an increase of three percentage points for X-category cities, two percentage points for Y-category cities and one percentage point for Z-category cities.

The actual additional amount payable will depend on an employee's basic salary and the applicable classification of their posting location.

VDA Crosses 25 Per Cent Threshold, Triggers HRA Revision

The allowance enhancement follows the revision of VDA for wage-board employees to 26.8 per cent, effective September 1, 2026.

Under the provisions of NCWA-XI, an increase in VDA beyond the specified 25 per cent level triggers a corresponding revision in HRA rates.

With the latest VDA adjustment taking the figure to 26.8 per cent, Coal India has implemented the revised housing allowance structure in accordance with the applicable wage agreement.

The HRA will continue to be calculated on basic pay, subject to existing eligibility requirements and the company's rules governing allowance payments.

HRA Benefit To Extend Across Coal India Subsidiaries

The revised rates cover eligible non-executive employees of Coal India and its subsidiaries, subject to the conditions specified in the office order.

These include Bharat Coking Coal Limited (BCCL), Central Coalfields Limited (CCL), Eastern Coalfields Limited (ECL), Mahanadi Coalfields Limited (MCL), Northern Coalfields Limited (NCL), South Eastern Coalfields Limited (SECL), Western Coalfields Limited (WCL) and Central Mine Planning and Design Institute Limited (CMPDIL).

Since the revised structure takes effect from September 1, 2026, eligible employees will be entitled to the enhanced allowance from that date, subject to payroll processing and applicable company guidelines.

The decision increases the housing allowance component of compensation for Coal India's eligible non-executive workforce. The extent of the financial benefit will vary depending on individual basic pay and the city category in which employees are posted.

data.title: Shiv Shivakumar Rejoins Burger King India Operator’s Board
data.description:
Shivakumar reconnects with Restaurant Brands Asia’s leadership as the company reports strong same-store growth.

Shiv Shivakumar, Operating Partner at Advent International and former chairman of Restaurant Brands Asia, the operator of Burger King India, rejoined the company’s board, sharing the update in a LinkedIn post last week.

In his post, Shivakumar said he was pleased to reconnect with the leadership team, including Raj Varman, Sumit Zaveri, and Namrata Tiwari, along with other board members and the company’s new investors. He also noted that the company had moved into a new office in Andheri, Mumbai.

Commenting on the company’s recent performance, Shivakumar wrote, “Last quarter was v good with 14 pc same store growth. Kudos.” The figure was shared by Shivakumar in his post.

Return To The Board

Shivakumar previously served as chairman of Restaurant Brands Asia from January 2019 to January 2024. His return brings back a board member with extensive experience across consumer businesses, brand management and corporate strategy.

Restaurant Brands Asia operates Burger King restaurants in India and has been working to strengthen the brand’s presence in the country’s competitive quick-service restaurant (QSR) market.

Shivakumar’s earlier association with the company coincided with a period of expansion for Burger King India, as the brand continued to build its store network and strengthen its position in the organised QSR segment.

Shivakumar currently serves as an Operating Partner at Advent International. Before joining Advent in 2023, he was Group Executive President for Corporate Strategy and Business Development at the Aditya Birla Group, a role he held from 2018 to 2022.

His career spans leadership positions at several major companies. He spent 19 years at Hindustan Unilever across sales, marketing and general management before becoming CEO of Philips India's consumer electronics division in 2003.

In 2006, he joined Nokia as Managing Director for India and later became Senior Vice President for Emerging Markets. He subsequently led PepsiCo India as Chairman and CEO from 2013 to 2017, overseeing its beverages, snacks and nutrition businesses.

Beyond his corporate roles, Shivakumar holds several advisory and governance positions, including roles with Power Grid Corporation of India, SHRM, The Economist and Penguin Random House India. He is also associated with academic institutions, including the Indian Institute of Management Udaipur and SPJIMR.

data.title: ELANTAS Beck India Appoints Supriya Bansal As Chief Financial Officer
data.description:
Bansal joins the company with over two decades of experience in finance leadership, business transformation, ESG and sustainability advisory

ELANTAS Beck India has appointed Supriya Bansal as its Chief Financial Officer (CFO), effective October 2026, according to a company post on LinkedIn.

Bansal brings over two decades of experience in finance leadership, business transformation, environmental, social and governance (ESG) advisory and sustainability. She will be based in Pune, Maharashtra.

Before joining ELANTAS Beck India, Bansal was Partner, Global Sustainability and Digital Transformation at AVA Insights from April 2023 to October 2026. In this role, she worked with organisations on process reviews, gap analyses and identifying solutions for business requirements.

She also served as an Independent Director at BSA Corporation between February and October 2026.

Earlier, Bansal was Director, Global Business Services at United Software Group Inc from November 2022 to April 2023, where she was responsible for establishing shared services operations.

She also worked as Director, Finance Shared Services at Apexon from March 2022 to November 2022.

Professional Qualifications

Bansal is a Chartered Accountant from India and a Chartered Management Accountant from the UK. She also holds the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants' (ACCA) Diploma in International Financial Reporting.

Her other credentials include certifications as an independent director and sustainability professional.

She completed her studies at the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India between 1996 and 2002 and pursued qualifications through the Chartered Institute of Management Accountants (CIMA) from 2007 to 2009.

data.title: Reliance Jewels Appoints Gopa Kumar To Lead Business
data.description:
The retail veteran joins Reliance Jewels after a seven-year stint as COO of Bhima Jewels, bringing over two decades of experience

Reliance Jewels, part of Reliance Retail, has appointed Gopa Kumar as Head of Reliance Jewels, bringing an experienced retail executive on board to lead the jewellery business. Kumar announced his new role through a LinkedIn post, stating that he was looking forward to building on the brand's legacy and identifying fresh opportunities for growth.

He joins Reliance Jewels after a seven-year stint as Chief Operating Officer at Bhima Jewels, where he had been associated with the retailer since 2019. During his tenure, he oversaw operations at the jewellery business before announcing his departure and return to Mumbai.

Kumar brings more than two decades of experience across organised retail and consumer-facing businesses. His professional background includes leadership positions at Future Group, Shoppers Stop, Hindustan Unilever, Next Retail and Future Retail, among others.

His experience spans business strategy, profit and loss management, retail operations, category management, marketing, digital initiatives and business expansion. He has also worked across different retail formats, including department stores, convenience retail, e-commerce, luxury, lifestyle and speciality retail.

At Reliance Jewels, Kumar is expected to focus on business strategy, retail expansion, brand development and customer experience, alongside driving revenue growth and operational performance. His responsibilities will also include strengthening merchandising and product strategy, digital and omnichannel initiatives, and organisational capabilities.

The appointment comes as Reliance Jewels continues to operate within India's organised jewellery retail market, with a portfolio spanning gold, diamond and silver jewellery and a nationwide network of company-owned showrooms.

data.title: IGL Q2 profit plunges 93% as higher gas costs erode margins despite record sales
data.description:
Indraprastha Gas Ltd (IGL), the country's largest city gas distributor, reported a sharp 93.5 per cent decline in standalone net profit for the September quarter as a substantial increase in input gas costs eroded margins, offsetting higher sales volumes and revenue.

Net profit fell to ₹24.38 crore in the second quarter of 2026-27 from ₹372.51 crore a year earlier, despite an 8 per cent increase in sales volumes and a 26 per cent jump in gross turnover.

The company said its average daily gas sales crossed the 10 million standard cubic metres per day (mmscmd) mark for the first time, rising to 10.06 mmscmd in the July-September period from 9.31 mmscmd in the corresponding period last year.

Gross sales turnover increased to ₹5,999.13 crore from ₹4,431.63 crore, reflecting higher sales as well as the impact of increased gas prices.

CNG volumes grew 9 per cent year-on-year during the quarter, while piped natural gas (PNG) sales rose 8 per cent, indicating continued expansion in demand across the transport and household segments.

However, the steep fall in profitability despite higher volumes and turnover highlights the pressure that rising procurement costs can exert on city gas distributors, particularly when increase in input prices cannot be fully passed on to consumers.

IGL operates city gas distribution networks across 34 districts in 11 geographical areas spanning Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Rajasthan.

Its infrastructure includes more than 30,000 km of pipelines and over 1,000 CNG stations, catering to more than 2.5 million CNG vehicles. It has also connected over 3.5 million households to piped natural gas.

data.title: Piyush Goyal Urges FMCG Firms To Join ONDC Push To Digitise 1.4 Cr Kirana Stores
data.description:
At a CEO roundtable in New Delhi, the minister calls for industry-wide collaboration to strengthen digital procurement, improve supply-chain efficiency and expand access to credit for neighbourhood retailers

Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has called on FMCG companies and industry stakeholders to work together to accelerate the digitalisation of India's 1.4 crore kirana stores, as the government steps up efforts to strengthen the country's general trade ecosystem through ONDC's DigiDukaan initiative.

Goyal chaired a high-level CEO roundtable, Bharat Commerce Chintan Shivir, organised by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) and the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) at Vanijya Bhawan, New Delhi. The meeting brought together more than 40 senior leaders from leading FMCG companies to discuss a common roadmap for digitising procurement and improving the competitiveness of neighbourhood retailers.

The discussions focused on securing greater institutional commitment from FMCG companies, distributors and other stakeholders to promote digital procurement, streamline supply chains and improve access to services for small retailers.

DigiDukaan Focuses On Digitising Procurement

Unlike conventional kirana digitisation initiatives that primarily help retailers sell products online, ONDC's DigiDukaan focuses on digitising them as buyers. The platform aims to enable neighbourhood stores to discover and order products from multiple brands, distributors and wholesalers through a single digital interface.

Retailers can access greater transparency on pricing, trade schemes and product availability while continuing to work with their existing distribution partners. The initiative also aims to create a common digital infrastructure that can eventually connect kiranas with shared logistics, micro-warehousing and formal credit facilities.

Senior representatives from Hindustan Unilever, Coca-Cola India, ITC, P&G, Marico, CavinKare, Pidilite, Britannia, Adani Wilmar, LT Foods, Anmol Industries, Haldiram's, Emami, Veeba and Nilon's attended the roundtable, along with logistics providers, technology partners and ONDC network participants.

Common Digital Identity, Logistics And Credit In Focus

The roundtable identified five key priorities for strengthening India's general trade ecosystem.

These include developing a common digital identity for kirana stores to facilitate seamless engagement with multiple brands and service providers; creating shared logistics and micro-warehousing infrastructure to improve distributor reach and enable reliable next-day replenishment; and expanding access to formal credit through financing solutions linked to digital procurement and transaction records.

The discussions also highlighted the need to simplify technology integration through plug-and-play Distributor Management System (DMS) connectors, standardised product catalogues and common digital interfaces.

Another key priority is realigning commercial incentives for FMCG sales teams, distributors and channel partners to encourage digital ordering, wider retail coverage and sustained adoption of the platform.

DigiDukaan Connects 21,000 Retailers With 450 Brands

DigiDukaan has connected more than 21,000 retailers with over 450 brands across Hyderabad, Jaipur and Mumbai as of September 2026, compared with over 12,000 retailers in the previous quarter.

Hyderabad accounts for more than 16,000 onboarded retailers, with monthly repeat ordering rates ranging between 73% and 78%. An initial ONDC study also found that 40% of surveyed retailers reported lower inventory holdings for products procured through DigiDukaan, indicating the potential for improved working capital efficiency.

Goyal said the initiative demonstrated how open digital infrastructure, designed around the needs of small retailers, could accelerate adoption.

"By making procurement simpler and more transparent while strengthening our distributors, we can help kiranas free up working capital and grow," he said, inviting the FMCG industry to work together to extend the initiative across the country. He also called for DigiDukaan to become a case study for the world to learn from India's digital commerce model.

DPIIT Secretary Amardeep Singh Bhatia said open digital infrastructure had an important role in accelerating the digitalisation of India's retail ecosystem, particularly its extensive network of kirana stores.

He said DigiDukaan demonstrated how an open and interoperable network could help neighbourhood retailers access digital procurement opportunities and participate more effectively in the evolving digital economy.

FMCG Brands And Technology Partners Expand Participation

ONDC Managing Director and CEO Vibhor Jain said that while distributors had increasingly adopted digital tools for billing, printing and order placement, many neighbourhood retailers continued to depend on manual processes.

DigiDukaan aims to address this gap by digitising kiranas as buyers while strengthening, rather than replacing, the existing distributor network, he said. Jain added that the objective was to create a shared digital foundation through which retailers could access multiple brands, transparent trade schemes, faster replenishment and, eventually, formal credit.

Among FMCG companies participating through their distribution networks are HUL, Marico, Colgate-Palmolive, Emami and Amul. ITC, Tata Consumer Products and Britannia are at various stages of integration or discussions.

On the technology front, Paytm for Business, Qwipo and Mulltiply.ai are live on the network, while Bizom, Botree, QuIDPe and ENS are progressing towards integration. Logistics and warehousing partners, including ElasticRun, Shiprocket, India Post and Moeving, are also part of the expanding ecosystem.

The National Traders' Welfare Board, chaired by Sunil J. Singhi, is working with ONDC to accelerate adoption among kirana retailers by mobilising local trade associations and strengthening retailer participation.

For its next phase, ONDC plans to deepen brand and distributor participation in Mumbai, particularly North Mumbai, while strengthening operations in its existing markets.

data.title: Sebi Fines CDSL Rs 1 Crore For Compliance Lapses
data.description:
The market regulator flags deficiencies in pledge request communication, cybersecurity controls, vulnerability patching and disaster recovery operations following an inspection for FY24

Markets regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has imposed a penalty of Rs 1 crore on Central Depository Services (India) (CDSL) for multiple regulatory compliance lapses, including deficiencies in pledge request communication, cybersecurity safeguards and disaster recovery operations.

In an adjudication order dated October 30, Sebi said its inspection of CDSL for FY2023-24 had revealed several instances of non-compliance with regulatory requirements. The depository has been directed to pay the penalty within 45 days, failing which recovery proceedings may be initiated.

Pledge Rejection Communication Under Scanner

One of the key violations related to CDSL's failure to communicate the reasons for rejecting pledge requests to the depository participants (DPs) of both the pledgor and the pledgee.

According to the findings reported in the adjudication proceedings, the regulator identified 92 instances of such failures during the inspection period. CDSL submitted that its earlier system did not make it mandatory to record rejection reasons. The company subsequently introduced system changes to address the deficiency.

Sebi also flagged non-compliance with prescribed procedures governing Client Unpaid Securities Accounts (CUSA). The shortcomings included deficiencies in freezing and unfreezing securities, inadequate system-level checks and failure to follow certain instructions issued by stock exchanges.

Cybersecurity And Disaster Recovery Lapses

The regulator also identified shortcomings in CDSL's information technology and cybersecurity framework.

These included inadequate measures to prevent unauthorised transmission of data and incomplete implementation of Data Loss Prevention safeguards. Sebi found that security information and event management logs were being collected at the primary data centre during a disaster recovery drill instead of the designated disaster recovery site.

Further, CDSL had failed to patch identified software vulnerabilities within the prescribed timeline. Its Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing (VAPT) exercise was also found to be inadequate, as it did not cover all relevant domains and external applications.

Sebi Flags Implications For Market Integrity

Emphasising the systemic importance of depositories, Sebi observed that the deficiencies affected CDSL's core responsibilities relating to electronic record-keeping, dematerialisation and securities ownership transfers.

The regulator noted that such lapses could have implications not only for individual investors but also for the integrity and stability of the Indian securities market.

Sebi, however, took note of the remedial measures subsequently undertaken by CDSL while determining the penalty. It imposed the Rs 1 crore fine under Section 15HB of the Sebi Act, 1992.

In July this year, Sebi had also imposed a separate Rs 1 crore penalty on CDSL over cybersecurity shortcomings linked to a malware attack that disrupted its systems in November 2022.

data.title: Ramkrishna Forgings Q2 Revenue Jumps 55% To Rs 1,405 Cr, PAT At Rs 71 Cr
data.description:
The EBITDA margin improved to 18.2 per cent from 13.5 per cent in the year-ago quarter, an expansion of 473 basis points

Ramkrishna Forgings reported a 54.9 per cent year-on-year (Y-o-Y) increase in consolidated revenue from operations to Rs 1,405.42 crore in the second quarter of financial year 2026-27 (Q2FY27), supported by healthy domestic demand and resilient export market activity.

The company's profit after tax (PAT) stood at Rs 70.59 crore in Q2FY27, compared with a loss of Rs 9.50 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year. PAT had stood at Rs 47 crore in the preceding quarter.

Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) more than doubled to Rs 256.23 crore in Q2FY27, compared with Rs 122.54 crore a year earlier, registering a growth of 109.1 per cent.

The EBITDA margin improved to 18.2 per cent from 13.5 per cent in the year-ago quarter, an expansion of 473 basis points.

For the first half of FY27, the company's consolidated revenue increased 36.4 per cent to Rs 2,622.09 crore, compared with Rs 1,922.79 crore in H1FY26.

EBITDA for the first half rose 75.1 per cent to Rs 474.70 crore, while the EBITDA margin improved to 18.1 per cent from 14.1 per cent in the corresponding period last year.

PAT for H1FY27 stood at Rs 117.47 crore, compared with Rs 2.29 crore in the year-ago period.

Commenting on the results, Naresh Jalan, Managing Director of Ramkrishna Forgings, said domestic demand remained healthy, supported by firm commercial vehicle production schedules, while customer activity across key export markets remained resilient.

The company is also expanding its manufacturing capabilities. Its forged wheels facility near Chennai, established through a joint venture with Titagarh Rail Systems, is nearing commercial production. The project is expected to expand its presence in the Indian Railways supply chain.

The company is also ramping up its casting operations and adding capacities and value-added products to serve customers across passenger vehicles, electric vehicles and industrial applications.

During the quarter, the promoters completed the conversion of warrants, infusing Rs 150 crore into the company to support its balance sheet and ongoing business requirements.

Looking ahead, Ramkrishna Forgings is seeking to expand its presence in non-ferrous forgings, including aluminium, titanium, Inconel and Nimonic grades. These materials are intended for high-technology applications across aerospace, robotics and semiconductors.

Jalan said the company's focus would remain on improving capacity utilisation, disciplined execution and strengthening its balance sheet as it pursues long-term growth opportunities.

data.title: Infosys Adds 10,000 Seats With 1.1 Mn Sq Ft Expansion In Hyderabad
data.description:
he 1.1 million sq ft expansion will add 10,000 seats at the 450-acre Pocharam campus, taking its total built-up area to 5.68 million sq ft and supporting over 13,000 additional employees under a hybrid work model.

Infosys has expanded its Pocharam Development Centre in Hyderabad with a new 1.1 million sq ft software development block, adding 10,000 seats as the IT services company looks to scale its operations and strengthen its technology delivery capabilities in Telangana.

The facility, inaugurated on Friday in the presence of Telangana Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka and IT and Industries Minister Duddilla Sridhar Babu, takes the company's built-up area at the 450-acre Pocharam campus to approximately 5.68 million sq ft.

The new block will enable Infosys to support an additional workforce of more than 13,000 employees under its hybrid working model, the company said in a statement.

The expansion comes as technology services companies look to strengthen their delivery capabilities in areas such as artificial intelligence (AI), cloud computing, cybersecurity and engineering, amid growing enterprise demand for digital transformation.

Infosys Chief Financial Officer Jayesh Sanghrajka said Hyderabad had played an important role in the company's growth and that the expanded facility would increase its capacity to scale operations and develop specialised talent.

"As enterprises accelerate their adoption of AI, the campus will serve as a strategic hub that brings together world-class talent, infrastructure and technology capabilities to deliver complex transformation programmes for global clients," Sanghrajka said.

The Pocharam Development Centre currently has seven software development blocks, with a combined built-up area of approximately 4.58 million sq ft. The latest addition will further expand its delivery footprint in Hyderabad.

The centre caters to global clients across banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI), retail, life sciences and manufacturing. Its expanded operations will focus on strengthening capabilities in AI, cloud, cybersecurity, engineering and next-generation digital services.

The facility also incorporates energy-efficient infrastructure, including radiant cooling systems, smart lighting, rainwater harvesting and wastewater reuse. It has been designed with natural daylight, flexible workspaces, collaborative areas and employee wellness facilities.

Vikramarka said the expansion reflected Hyderabad's growing position as a destination for global technology companies, supported by infrastructure development and a skilled workforce.

"Investments of this scale reinforce Hyderabad's position as a preferred destination for global enterprises and advance our vision of a future-ready, innovation-driven economy," he said.

data.title: Aditya Birla Capital Q2 Profit Jumps 38%, Housing Finance PBT Surges 73%
data.description:
NBFC disbursements rose 12 per cent as overall lending assets expanded to Rs 2.34 lakh crore by September-end

Aditya Birla Capital reported a 38 per cent year-on-year increase in consolidated profit attributable to owners to Rs 1,288 crore for the September quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 933.5 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. The growth was supported by expansion across its lending and financial services businesses.

Consolidated revenue from operations rose 32.2 per cent year on year to Rs 14,003 crore from Rs 10,594 crore a year earlier. On a sequential basis, profit increased 9.62 per cent from Rs 1,174.70 crore in the June quarter, while revenue grew 14.97 per cent from Rs 12,179.54 crore.

Total expenses increased 30.07 per cent year on year to Rs 12,324.10 crore during the quarter, compared with Rs 9,474.99 crore in the year-ago period. Sequentially, expenses rose 15.27 per cent from Rs 10,691.74 crore recorded in the June quarter.

The company’s overall lending assets under management, covering its NBFC and housing finance businesses, increased 32 per cent year on year and 7 per cent sequentially to Rs 2,33,930 crore as of September 30, 2026. Both businesses recorded higher AUM and disbursements during the quarter.

The NBFC business reported a 26 per cent year-on-year increase in AUM to Rs 1,76,557 crore, while disbursements rose 12 per cent to Rs 24,708 crore. Profit before tax increased 41 per cent year on year to Rs 1,352 crore during the September quarter.

Housing finance recorded faster growth, with AUM rising 50 per cent year on year and 11 per cent sequentially to Rs 57,373 crore. Disbursements increased 55 per cent year on year and 19 per cent sequentially to Rs 8,957 crore, while profit before tax rose 73 per cent to Rs 335 crore.

Asset Management Performance

In asset management, quarterly average mutual fund AUM increased 4 per cent year on year to Rs 4,41,787 crore during the quarter. Equity quarterly average AUM grew 9 per cent to Rs 2,09,230 crore, while profit after tax for the business stood at Rs 221 crore.

The company also reported growth across its insurance businesses during the first half of FY27. Individual first-year premium in life insurance increased 25 per cent year on year to Rs 2,342 crore, while gross written premium in health insurance rose 48 per cent to Rs 4,543 crore.

Aditya Birla Capital’s digital platforms also expanded during the quarter, with its direct-to-consumer platform ABCD recording around 1.3 crore customer acquisitions as of September 30, 2026. The company’s business-to-business platform Udyog Plus crossed 24 lakh registrations.

Udyog Plus, which caters to the micro, small and medium enterprises ecosystem, had an AUM of Rs 7,262 crore at the end of the quarter. Across its businesses, Aditya Birla Capital had a network of 1,822 branches as of September 30.

Shares of Aditya Birla Capital ended 2.19 per cent higher at Rs 366.20 on October 30, gaining Rs 7.85 during the session. The stock has risen 2.17 per cent year to date and 16.91 per cent over the past year.

data.title: Jio Platforms Reports 14% Q2 Profit Growth In First Results After IPO
data.description:
Revenue from operations rises 11.4 per cent to Rs 40,475 crore as 5G subscribers cross 300 million and fixed broadband base reaches 30 million

Jio Platforms has delivered double-digit growth in profit and revenue in its first quarterly results since its stock market listing, with consolidated profit after tax (PAT) rising 13.7 per cent year on year to Rs 8,387 crore in Q2 FY27. The company, which raised Rs 30,188 crore through its initial public offering (IPO), reported its results two days after its shares began trading on the stock exchanges on 28 October.

Revenue from operations increased 11.4 per cent to Rs 40,475 crore in the September quarter, against Rs 36,332 crore in the corresponding period last year. The figure was also 3.3 per cent higher than the Rs 39,173 crore recorded in Q1 FY27.

Profit after tax increased 8 per cent sequentially from Rs 7,764 crore in the June quarter. Gross revenue, which includes revenue beyond operations, stood at Rs 47,485 crore, up 11.3 per cent year on year from Rs 42,652 crore and 3.3 per cent quarter on quarter from Rs 45,961 crore.

The earnings growth came alongside an improvement in operating margins. Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) rose 16.6 per cent year on year to Rs 21,879 crore from Rs 18,757 crore. On a sequential basis, Ebitda increased 4.9 per cent from Rs 20,865 crore.

Ebitda margin expanded to 54.1 per cent from 51.6 per cent a year earlier, a gain of 250 basis points. The margin was 53.3 per cent in the preceding quarter. Jio Platforms attributed the improvement to revenue growth, operating leverage and a stronger margin profile.

Earnings And Cash Generation

Profit before tax (PBT) increased 13.3 per cent year on year to Rs 11,259 crore from Rs 9,937 crore. The figure was 8 per cent higher than the Rs 10,427 crore reported in Q1 FY27.

Earnings before interest and tax (Ebit) grew 18.1 per cent to Rs 14,268 crore from Rs 12,082 crore in Q2 FY26. Its margin rose 200 basis points year on year to 35.3 per cent.

For the six months ended September 2026, revenue from operations reached Rs 79,648 crore, against Rs 71,364 crore in the corresponding period last year, an increase of 11.6 per cent. PAT rose 11.5 per cent to Rs 16,151 crore from Rs 14,485 crore, while Ebitda increased 15.9 per cent to Rs 42,744 crore from Rs 36,892 crore.

Cash generation also improved. Ebitda less cash capital expenditure stood at Rs 32,130 crore in the first half of FY27, nearly double the Rs 16,216 crore reported in the year-ago period. The company defines cash capital expenditure as cash outflow on property, plant and equipment, spectrum and other intangible assets, net of disposal proceeds.

5G And Broadband Expansion

Jio Platforms' customer base reached 542.4 million at the end of September, compared with 506.4 million a year earlier. The company added 9.1 million customers during the quarter, against 8.3 million in Q2 FY26. Monthly churn declined to 1.6 per cent from 1.9 per cent in the year-ago quarter.

Average revenue per user (ARPU) increased 3.5 per cent year on year to Rs 218.8 from Rs 211.4. It also rose from Rs 215.6 in Q1 FY27. The company said promotional offers for fixed broadband customers partly offset the benefits of a better subscriber mix and higher usage.

The 5G subscriber base crossed 300 million in September, with 66 million additions over the preceding 12 months. The technology accounted for around 56 per cent of Jio's total wireless traffic.

The fixed broadband base reached 30 million subscribers, following the addition of 7.3 million connections over the past year. Jio AirFiber accounted for 15.1 million of these subscribers and contributed more than 75 per cent of fixed broadband additions during the period.

Data consumption continued to rise alongside subscriber growth. Total data traffic increased 22.1 per cent year on year to 71.3 billion GB in Q2 FY27. Monthly data consumption per customer reached 44.2 GB, compared with 38.7 GB in the corresponding quarter last year.

IPO Proceeds And Debt

Jio Platforms' market debut on 28 October marked its entry into the listed market. The IPO, which comprised a fresh issue of 27 crore equity shares at Rs 1,119 apiece, generated gross proceeds of Rs 30,188 crore after the employee discount.

The company has allocated a substantial portion of the net proceeds towards reducing borrowings at its material subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm. Jio Platforms said Rs 27,500 crore had been used to repay, either fully or partly, the principal outstanding on certain external commercial borrowings. The remaining proceeds will go towards general corporate purposes, in accordance with the IPO prospectus.

The company is also positioning its digital services portfolio around emerging technologies. At India Mobile Congress 2026, it showcased Jio Call Agent, an artificial intelligence-based tool that can transcribe and summarise calls, and JioFrames, a smart camera product with voice assistance, live translation and other connected features.

Jio Platforms Managing Director Akash M Ambani said the latest results reflected the expansion of the company's 5G network and broadband and digital services. He also identified satellite communications, 6G intellectual property and artificial intelligence integration across voice and data services as areas for future investment.

data.title: Syrma SGS Q2 Net Profit Jumps 87%, Revenue Rises 73%
data.description:
Strong automotive, industrial and export demand drives record quarterly performance, with exports jumping 91 per cent despite industry-wide component supply constraints.

Syrma SGS Technology posted its highest-ever quarterly performance in the September quarter of FY27, with consolidated net profit rising 87.2 per cent year-on-year to Rs 124.2 crore, supported by strong growth across its automotive, industrial and export businesses.

Revenue from operations increased 73.2 per cent to Rs 1,999.5 crore in the second quarter, compared with the year-ago period, while earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) rose 63.9 per cent to Rs 203.1 crore from Rs 124 crore, according to the company's earnings release dated October 30.

The electronics systems design and manufacturing (ESDM) company attributed the growth to robust demand from the automotive and industrial segments, alongside a sharp rise in exports, despite industry-wide component supply constraints.

Jasbir Singh Gujral, Managing Director at Syrma SGS Technology, said the company had reached the milestone of Rs 2,000 crore in quarterly revenue while navigating component shortages across the industry.

Exports emerged as a major growth driver, with revenue from overseas markets climbing 91 per cent year-on-year to Rs 513.8 crore. Exports accounted for 26 per cent of operating revenue during the quarter.

Among business segments, automotive revenue grew 91 per cent to Rs 516.9 crore, contributing 26 per cent to operating revenue, compared with 24 per cent in the corresponding quarter last year.

The industrials business recorded an 86 per cent increase in revenue to Rs 493.5 crore, accounting for 25 per cent of operating revenue.

The consumer segment remained the company's largest business by revenue, growing 57 per cent to Rs 572.7 crore. However, its contribution to operating revenue declined to 29 per cent from 32 per cent a year earlier.

Revenue from the IT and railways segment rose 69 per cent to Rs 272.7 crore, while healthcare revenue increased 61 per cent to Rs 134 crore.

Despite the strong revenue and profit growth, the company reported a sequential moderation in operating margins. EBITDA margin stood at 10.2 per cent in the September quarter, compared with 11 per cent in the June quarter. The profit after tax (PAT) margin also declined to 6.2 per cent from 6.6 per cent sequentially.

On a year-on-year basis, EBITDA margin contracted 58 basis points, while PAT margin improved 47 basis points.

Commenting on the first-half performance, Gujral said revenue grew 71 per cent and profit after tax nearly doubled, reflecting the company's execution capabilities.

He added that Syrma SGS had fulfilled customer commitments while reducing its working capital cycle to 63 days and turning operating cash flow positive during the first half of FY27.

data.title: CCI Clears Prosus’ $100 Mn Investment In Sachin Bansal-Led Navi
data.description:
Sachin Bansal, cofounder and executive chairman of Navi, said the partnership was significant given his association with Naspers and the Prosus Group spanning more than a decade

The Competition Commission of India (CCI) has approved Prosus’ investment in Navi, allowing the global investment firm to acquire a minority stake in the fintech company founded by Sachin Bansal.

The approval follows Prosus’ USD 100 million investment in Navi, which marked the startup’s first institutional fundraise. The transaction was subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions.

As per a media report, the CCI described Navi as the holding company of a group offering financial services through a single consumer-facing mobile application. Its subsidiaries provide digital financial products accessible through mobile devices.

Navi did not disclose the valuation at which Prosus invested, the stake being acquired or the planned use of the funds.

Sachin Bansal, cofounder and executive chairman of Navi, said the partnership was significant given his association with Naspers and the Prosus Group spanning more than a decade. He added that the investment reflected confidence in the financial services institution the company was building.

Prosus said it was backing Navi because of its large user base, multiple business lines and technology-led approach. Ashutosh Sharma, head of Prosus India investments and M&A, noted that the company had delivered strong execution over the previous 12 months despite a challenging macroeconomic environment.

During FY26, Navi UPI strengthened its position in digital payments, while its lending arm, Navi Finserv, expanded its loan portfolio, with assets under management (AUM) crossing Rs 13,000 crore. The group also reported consolidated profitability in the fourth quarter of FY26, although it did not disclose the figures.

Navi Finserv's standalone net profit increased 32 per cent year-on-year to Rs 292.2 crore in FY26, while operating revenue rose 8 per cent to Rs 2,461 crore. However, its consolidated net profit declined 46 per cent to Rs 93.3 crore, even as operating revenue grew 17 per cent to Rs 2,691.5 crore.

Navi's IPO Plans

The investment comes as Navi is reportedly preparing to revive its public listing plans. As per a media report, the fintech company is considering refiling its draft IPO papers with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) by December 2026.

The proposed offering is expected to include a fresh issue of around Rs 3,000 crore. Navi has reportedly appointed JM Financial, Kotak Mahindra Capital, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan as advisers for the planned IPO.

This would be Navi's second attempt to go public. The company filed draft papers with SEBI in 2022 for a Rs 3,350 crore IPO but later shelved the plan amid unfavourable market conditions.

Founded in 2018 by Sachin Bansal and Ankit Agarwal, Navi offers financial products across lending, insurance, mutual funds and UPI payments. Bansal stepped down as CEO in February 2025 and took over as executive chairman.

Navi said its UPI platform remained India's fourth-largest third-party application provider by transaction volume during FY26. Meanwhile, Navi Finserv's AUM crossed Rs 13,000 crore.
